cells.tense: You are at the work of keeping or releasing what this group passes on, and your hands are on it now.
cells.ask: Hand one finished thing to one person today, out loud — a story, a recipe, a rule the group still uses — and tell them why you kept it.
cells.core:
You're at the work of what this group keeps and what it lets go. An old way or an old story comes up, and it's clear to you whether it still feeds anyone or whether it's just sitting there. You don't make a speech about it. You take the useful parts, leave the rest, and what you pass on still works for the people who get it.

That's a real service, and the cost is that it's mostly invisible — nobody thanks you for the things you quietly stopped carrying. Fairness matters here in a practical way: keep the give and take actually moving, and notice when you're the only one holding the shovel.

cells.tense: You are out ahead of the room, deciding what this group should keep or drop before anyone has said what it means to them.
cells.ask: Leave one thing standing this week — a practice, an object, a gathering — and let it run one more time. Say out loud that you're leaving it.
cells.core:
You can see where this group needs to end up, and you're already clearing the path. You mention what should change before anyone has finished saying what it means to them — a tradition, the way a thing has been done, a room people know. It isn't wrong, exactly. It's just early, and people feel the early part even when they agree with the destination.

What you're after is a group that holds together through a change rather than scattering when the ground moves. So let this one thing breathe before you touch it. Tell someone you're holding off, so the waiting reads as a choice you made instead of something that happened to you.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided what goes before anyone's said what it's worth.

cells.tense: Something got dropped back there — a decision about what this group carries, or a change you meant to make — and you're still standing where you left it.
cells.ask: Do one small act of upkeep today with someone watching — fix the thing, teach the thing, sort the thing — and let them see you do it.
cells.core:
Something needed handling in what this group keeps, and you didn't pick it up. The old way still sits there, or a thing you stopped tending still sits there, and people are working around it. It leaves a mark on the day you notice in passing — and then you pass.

What's short right now isn't care. It's the push to begin. You don't need to know how it ends; you need one reason you actually feel. Start from that one. Pick the piece you'd be glad to see working again and give it an hour, not a plan. Wanting has to come first here. Duty alone won't move it.

cells.tense: You are the one already sorting what this group keeps and what it lets go, whether or not you have said so.
cells.ask: Call one thing yours today — say 'this is my call' about a practice or a decision you've been treating as just how things are.
cells.core:
You've been taking the blackout curtains down before anyone else moves, and no one asked you to. The weight of the old is still here, and you're the one whose hands are on whether it stays or goes. You sort it quietly — what gets kept, what gets renamed, what gets left behind. When you do that well, the people around you know what still stands without being told.

So the good version of this is steady rather than loud: a call made once, cleanly, and held. What waits underneath is permission you keep expecting from somewhere else. It isn't coming from out there. Say one of these calls is yours, and the floor stops shifting under the people around you.

attempts.check: The record says the card composes old material into conditions for new growth, but nothing in it says this person runs anything or formally stewards a tradition — the reader could reasonably say they have no such role and no one asked their opinion. The ask does not need the role to be real, because handing on a piece of the common stock is something anyone in a family, a shift, or a friend group can do today. The sentence that serves the writer is any version of 'you pick what gets carried forward' — that flatters a role I cannot see, so it stays out. Narrowed claims kept: one event, one recipient, one handed-on thing; nothing about history, motive, or what this person is underneath.

The asks survive that objection because each one is a single small act any person can do inside a family, a friend group or a shift, and none of them depends on the role being recognized.
